text.p: Belgian bank Kredietbank (KB), due to release 1996 results after Thursday's bourse close, benefitted from renewed investor interest in the Belgian banking sector, dealers said on Thursday.
Bucking the market trend, Kredietbank was up 0.2 percent at 13,225 francs at 1205 GMT in lively trade. The Bel-20 share index eased 0.8 percent.
The share has gained almost 11 percent since speculation about a merger between Belgian rivals BBL and Generale Bank took centre-stage in late February.
There has also been recent speculation that Kredietbank might announce an alliance with French bank Credit Commercial de France CCF

"I would prefer a merger between KB and CCF over one between Generale Bank and BBL because it would give a Belgian bank direct access to the foreign market where there's more business to be made," said a trader.
"KB (stock) is higher because everyone is waiting for the 1996 results and it's possible they might surprise the market and announce an alliance," he added.
Kredietbank earnings are forecast to have risen by 10 to 13 percent in 1996.
Generale Bank said earlier this week 1996 group net rose by 10 percent to 15.1 billion francs. BBL net profit grew by 15 percent to 10.3 billion francs.
